scores.breakdown:
Hook 8.5/10 · Energy/escalation 13/15 · Rhythm/silences/peak 13/15 · Angles 9.5/10 · Motif/match cuts 9/10 · Story (problem→solution) 14/15 · Sag-proofing 6.5/10 · Type 7/10 · Facts/buildability 4/5.

HOOK: The frame-0 macro clay streak has a transient, then top-down cascade, FPV, worm's-eye ziggurat: 4 cuts by 2.0, BRAAM + card at 2.0, a question at 4.0, rewind with tape-stop. It is textbook. The braam card is the weak link: 'THE LAST WAVE / TOOK ≈5 MONTHS.' is 7 words on two lines while the shot slams. A 2-word mega slam hits harder.

STORY: This is the best argument of the three, and the only one with real causality for 'coding agents aren't enough'. Code at agent speed (#36) slams into human-speed stations (#37–43). THE LINE WAITS. → the reflex 'just add more agents.' (#49, typed in the V1 voice) → two writers crack one card (#52) → ×17.2 → silence → who runs the line? An exec can retell it.

ENERGY: It escalates on 7 axes: tempo 120→150 at 86.0, ASL 1.2→0.93→0.74 (peak 0.2), scale (1→10→100→1,000 orbs; human 1:166), cold→warm, handheld/Dutch→level/symmetric, 2.39→full-frame letterbox, and a dark hall→lights on. The turn at 89.2 (#82) is the best frame in any treatment. It fires the mirror of #38, the refrain flip WAITS→RUNS, the Dutch righting to 0, the letterbox snapping open and BRAAM #2 on one frame. The lights-on banks (#78–81, one per 150-BPM beat with pitched clunks) are pure trailer awe.

RHYTHM: Silences at 38.0 (0.5 s, on the midpoint), 82.0 (1.0 s, drop) and 118.0 (0.8 s, false stop). Braams at 2.0, 89.2 and 118.8. Peak 113.2–117.6 = 84.7–88.0% ✓, title at 88.9% ✓. Best syncopation in the set: 0.4 s stillness → light with NO sound → '5.5' on the delayed boom (#94–96).

ANGLES: Deliberate, meaningful alternation. Worm's-eye = threat (towers), then awe (foreman). Top-down = understanding (midpoint, factory, graph). Macro inserts at 0.4 s between the tricolon cards.

MOTIFS: The richest mirror system: 38→82, 39/41/43→91–93, 53→90, 48→113, 1/2/4→108–110, 9→111/123. The human silhouette is the only emotional anchor in any treatment. But there are almost no true shape match cuts: every transition is a hard cut.

SAG POINTS:
(1) 64.5–74.0: after ×17.2 lands, ~9.5 s of 'more chaos' (#54–60: lock gate, human surrounded, FPV swarm, wildfire, cathedral, tower tips, breath) at a uniform 1.0 s, and then the accelerando is MORE chaos. Act II runs 38 s (28% of runtime) of red/cold; this is where an exec glances at their phone.
(2) 8–30: the music is drone + ticks + Risset only; there is no pulse until 30 and no ostinato until 44.
(3) 32–38: victory lap around the orb tower (#27–33) after the point has landed.
(4) 103.6–113.2: proof volley at 2.0/2.0/1.6/1.6/1.6, ending on a two-bar column, which is a bar chart (#104–105).
(5) Button: two 3 s holds.

TYPE: The refrain is the best copy device in the set. REVIEW./TEST./DEPLOY. are stamped in 3D at +20%/+40% sizes, then recalled white at 0.4 s, which is legit for primed words. Weaknesses: ~147 on-screen words by my count (claims 137) and text in ~54% of shot-time (target 35–40%). '#35 Coding: 16% of dev time.' is in sentence case, out of voice. Under-read: #47 'blocked on review.' typed in 1.0 s; #105 40% card at 1.6 s with 6 words + tag; #12 date at 0.5 s.

BUILD: It is the most buildable: pillars, towers, gates and banks are glowBox + beam + fog + bloom.
fatal_flaws: Problem act is 38 s with a ~9.5 s chaos plateau (64.5–74) that repeats one idea at uniform 1.0 s cuts. It is the 'wall of noise' numbness the client will feel as slow.
No pulse/ostinato until 0:30–0:44: the first 30+ s rides on drone and ticks. For a client who said 'very slow… bam bam bam', that is a risk at the most important retention window after the hook.

#35 geometry contradicts the card: CODE is station 3 of 7, but the sweep 'stops after 16% of its length' from the line start, which would light PLAN, not CODE. The CODE segment must be lit in place, sized at 16% of the line.

scores.breakdown:
Hook 9/10 · Energy 11/15 · Rhythm 11/15 · Angles 9/10 · Motif 8.5/10 · Story 10.5/15 · Sag-proofing 5.5/10 · Type 7/10 · Facts/buildability 3/5.

HOOK: The grandest frame-0→2 s of the three: the spark streaks a black particle sea, then a worm's-eye colossal curling wall overhead (#4), then BRAAM with '≈5 MONTHS.' assembling from spray (2 words, instantly legible). 'THE FIRST WAVE.' (#7) opens exactly the right loop, and it speaks the client's own language ('wave').

STORY: Act I has a real physical arc. A spark becomes a swell, passes 5 gates at truly accelerating intervals (18.5/21.5/~24/26.25/27.25) and grows 5 m→20 m, then breaks over the city at 38 (ASL 1.14, mood change #1 at 16.0, which puts a beat under the first wave early: good). The midpoint is the best storytelling device in the set. The tsunami draw-back (56–64) leads into 'that's not the horizon.', and a ridge planted 3 times by telephoto compression is revealed as a wave 50× bigger, on 0.5 s silence → BRAAM #2 → letterbox opening.

BUT the metaphor fights the thesis. A wave is an unstructured natural force; the argument is engineered structure and a delivery LINE. The line is never built on screen, yet 'THE WHOLE LINE.' (#110) pays it off. The drain-back (#39) reads as the first wave receding, which is false. A tsunami breaking over a city of desks with tiny people (#38, #107) reads as 'AI wipes out your workforce', which is the wrong tone for an Anthropic exec launch. It also has two competing reveals: braam #2 goes to the CONCEPT (64), while the PRODUCT reveal at 92 gets only an impact.

SAG: Act III-A (64–82) is the slowest act in the film (ASL 1.22) right after the biggest moment. Six consecutive 2.0 s shots each carry a card (IT'S THE NEXT WAVE / SOFTWARE FACTORY / GRAPH / HIERARCHY / SWARM / ×4.4), with no inserts and uniform spacing. That is the slideshow cadence the client rejected. Also 56–64 (four 2 s shots, sanctioned but long) and 123–127 (typed 3 s).

RHYTHM: Silences at 63.5, 89 and 119.2. Peak 113.6–116.8 = 84–86.5% ✓, title at 88.9% ✓. The 107 mirror (the second wave breaks where the first broke) is a strong peak image.

TYPE: Great V1 line ('that's not the horizon.'). 'OPUS 5.5' on screen at 93.6 (69%) dilutes the title drop. The end card repeats the title lockup. Under-read: #31 75% card (5 words + tag in 1.5 s), #97 40% card in 1.2 s, #110 in 0.8 s.

BUILD: It is the riskiest. A readable, grand curling wave and a barrel FPV from ≤30k points in SwiftShader at 0.75× is a real gamble, and the Interstellar misread only works if the ridge reads at phone size.
fatal_flaws: Act III-A (64–82): six back-to-back 2.0 s card shots at ASL 1.22, slower than Acts I and II, immediately after the braam. Anti-escalation at the turn.
Mixed metaphor: a wave is the opposite of 'structure', and the delivery line is never established, yet 'THE WHOLE LINE.' (#110) pays it off.
Brand/tone: a tsunami breaking over a city of desks with people (#38, #107) reads as AI destroying the workforce. The drain-back (#39) implies wave one receded, which contradicts the facts.
'OPUS 5.5' card at 93.6 (#86) spends the name 26 s before the title, and the product reveal gets a smaller hit than the concept reveal.

scores.breakdown:
Hook 8/10 · Energy 9.5/15 · Rhythm 10.5/15 · Angles 9/10 · Motif 9/10 · Story 11.5/15 · Sag-proofing 4.5/10 · Type 6.5/10 · Facts/buildability 4.5/5.

HOOK: The same template choreography (macro, top-down, FPV, worm's-eye, braam) with '≈5 MONTHS.' as a 2-word mega slam (good). Then 'CAPABILITY → BUDGET.' and 'THAT WAS WAVE ONE.' at 1.0 s each: under read time, and it spends the Act IIA payoff in the cold open (self-cannibalism). 'THAT WAS WAVE ONE.' is still a great line. The rewind collapsing to ONE cursor with a match cut on its rectangle (#9) is the cleanest transition idea in the set. The imagery (rectangles everywhere) is the least grand of the three and risks reading as a screensaver.

MOTIF: The best single-shape throughline for a technical audience: blink = human speed; double-time blink when Opus 4.5 ships (#21); a cursor city, cursors piled at walls, the monolith, the title slot; finally the cursor stops blinking and stays ON (#115). That last image is the best button in any treatment. It also has the most camera variety: whips ×3, log zoom (#19), dolly zoom (#33), orbits.

STORY: Cleanly ordered. The answer (coordinator → graph/hierarchy/swarm → THE SOFTWARE FACTORY, left unpowered) comes BEFORE the drop, so Act III is product + proof. But the problem is thin: the 84% is just 'walls'. There is no causal 'agent-speed code jams human-speed stations', and Act I spends 16 s establishing 'humans are slow', which is not the thesis.

ENERGY: It runs backwards where it matters. Act I ASL is 1.71 (eleven of its 14 shots are 1.5–2.0 s). The gates (+5/+8/+19 WEEKS at 34/38/42.5) are spaced 4.0/4.5 s, so they DON'T accelerate, despite #35 claiming 'now 2 s apart'. The climax act (ASL 0.91) is slower than the act before it (0.83) because every proof is a 2.4 s read-safe hold.

SAG POINTS:
(1) 12–24: human-speed cursors, desks, ticket walls, log zoom. This is the v1 slowness all over again.
(2) 35–37: a 2 s typed Karpathy quote stalls the gate run.
(3) 80–86: building a dark, unpowered wireframe factory, with little to look at.
(4) 100–112: proof volley of four 2.4 s cards at the climax.

RHYTHM: 3 silences + 3 braams placed correctly. Peak at 115.2 = 86.7% ✓, title at 88.6% ✓. The wordless visual tricolon (#107) is a nice touch. The 8×3 f recall flurry (#109) at 10 images/s is noise plus flash risk.

TYPE: Under-read: '+8 WEEKS / claude-pilled · WSJ' in 1.0 s; 'FABLE 5.1-LEVEL WORK. → −40% COST VS OPUS 5' as two cards in one 2.4 s shot. FACTS: the most faithful wording (verbatim 'PICKED THEIR OWN STRUCTURE.', 'FROM ONE HUMAN BRIEF'), and the 12-cluster/flat-sheet snap (#95–96) matches the system card exactly. But the protagonist cursor becomes the Google-study coordinator (#62), which ties a generic research result to Claude.
fatal_flaws: Act I (8–32) at ASL 1.71 with a 12 s human-speed establishing run (#12–19). This repeats the exact slowness the client rejected.
The climax act cuts slower (ASL 0.91) than Act IIC (0.83): four 2.4 s read-safe proof holds at 100–112 kill the bam-bam where the client wants the most.
Month/week gates at 34/38/42.5 don't accelerate, so the '5 months felt as acceleration' device fails on screen.
The weakest problem causality: 'other 84%' is shown as walls, not as code arriving at agent speed and jamming human-speed stations.

steal: BASE = machine. Keep its spine and set pieces intact: #34→#35 pull-back + 16% reveal; #36–#43 agent-speed cards jamming human-speed stations, with escalating red REVIEW./TEST./DEPLOY. stamps; #49 typed 'just add more agents.'; #52 two writers crack one card.

machine #38/#48 → #82: THE LINE WAITS ×2 → THE LINE RUNS on the identical mirror frame, with Dutch righting to 0 + letterbox snap + BRAAM #2 + 2 f flash. This is the film's signature frame; protect it.
machine #78–#81: lights-on, overhead banks slamming on one per 150-BPM beat with pitched clunks into the 89.2 braam.
machine #94–#98: 0.4 s stillness → clay light sweep with NO sound → '5.5' engraving on the delayed tier-S boom → core ignites → low-angle foreman with the human silhouette lit at its foot.
machine #88–#89: the swarm fans out to READ in parallel and converges on ONE writer that stamps. It is the only literal picture of 'parallelize reading, one writer per change'.
machine #53 → #90: locked top-down mirror where the ×17.2 tendrils retract to ×4.4. Add wave #68's '— SAME STUDY' tag, and make the coordinator a neutral ivory node, not brand clay.

machine #14–#24 + #25: MONTH gates at truly accelerating intervals (4/3/2.5/2 s) with Risset ticks, then the Halloran ride up the run-rate column. Add wave #28's shape match: the MONTH 5 gate ring closes onto the column base.
machine #48 → #113 and #9 → #111/#123: the human-under-red-tower frame returns lit amber at the peak; the Act I hall returns in the button.
wave #16 (music): bring the pulse ostinato in at 0:16 on OPUS 4.5 SHIPS. Machine's first 30–44 s run on drone + ticks, which is the biggest 'slow' risk.
signal #5 + #8: replace machine #5's 7-word two-line braam card with the 2-word mega slam '≈5 MONTHS.' on BRAAM #1, then 'THAT WAS WAVE ONE.' (hold ≥1.5 s) as the L1 opener before the rewind.

signal #9: the rewind collapses to ONE clay cursor ▮ and match-cuts on its rectangle into Act I. Carry the rectangle match chain cursor → MONTH gate opening → lit CODE box → title slot, since Machine has almost no true match cuts.
signal #21: the cursor 'breaks the tick' and blinks double time the moment Opus 4.5 ships (picture and sound go from human speed to agent speed). Use it in machine #13.
signal #38–#40: the cursor drops into a ledger slot and a 3D budget row is stamped clay with a dust burst, giving Machine's CAPABILITY → BUDGET (#26) a diegetic budget object instead of a bare card.

signal #95–#96: exactly 100 orbs snap into 12 sub-lead clusters, then the same 100 snap flat, with the verbatim card '100-AGENT TEAMS PICKED THEIR OWN STRUCTURE. · SYSTEM CARD' (replaces machine #99).
signal #89: a 0.4 s macro insert in the mirror tour. A work card passes the gate ice-in, clay-out.
signal #107: a wordless visual tricolon (three stations slam on, one per beat, escalating hit layers) immediately before the peak flash.

signal #115 + #116: after machine #123's MONTH 0 → MONTH 1, end on the lone cursor that blinks 3× on the tick, then stops blinking and stays ON with the final sting. Use signal's exact credit: 'MADE WITH CLAUDE OPUS 5.5 AGENTS / FROM ONE HUMAN BRIEF'.
signal #34/#61/#97: 2–3 whip transitions (360° shutter) in Acts II–III to break up Machine's all-hard-cut grammar.

wave #4/#8/#11/#31 → #59 (plant-and-misread): plant Machine's dark ziggurat from cold-open #4 as unexplained, telephoto-compressed background architecture in the hall 3 times (e.g. behind #9, #26, #60), so the foreman reveal at #98 pays off a plant.

wave #72: a top-down log zoom from one orb → a lane → the whole lit floor, with 'INSIDE ANTHROPIC: ~30,000 AGENTS AT ONCE.' (labelled, never tied to Opus 5.5). Put it right after THE SOFTWARE FACTORY as on-screen evidence that the next wave has started.
wave #64: type as architecture. Lanes of light bend to spell THE SOFTWARE FACTORY for machine #83.
wave #10: end the rewind on a 1px HDR light line and let that same line become the conveyor hairline (machine #34) and the title forge (machine #122).
cut: machine #55, #56, #58 (and shorten #60): collapse the 64.5–74 chaos plateau by ~4 s. Keep #54 lock-gate jam, #57 wildfire top-down and #59 tower-tip speed ramp, then go straight into the accelerando.
machine #48: trim the 3.0 s designated hold to 2.0 s (90 f is over the post-0:28 cap).
machine #19 (greeked newsprint panes, meaningless texture) and #31 (4,096-cursor city, off-metaphor); trim the 32–38 victory lap to ~4 s.
machine #5: the 7-word, two-line braam card 'THE LAST WAVE / TOOK ≈5 MONTHS.'
machine #35: the sentence-case 'Coding: 16% of dev time.' is out of voice; restyle it as narrator caps 'CODE: 16% OF DEV TIME. · ATLASSIAN'. Never sweep 16% from the line start (that lights PLAN).
machine #34: seven station labels (PLAN…OPERATE) decoding in ~1 s; keep them as non-read whisper texture or cut to 5.
machine #104–#105: the two-bar cost column, which is a bar chart. Restage it physically and give the 40% card ≥2.0 s.
machine #99 wording 'SELF-ORGANIZED.' and #126 wording 'MADE BY OPUS 5.5 AGENTS. ONE BRIEF.'
machine #12 'NOV 24 2025' as a standalone 0.5 s card: fold it into #13 as a kicker under OPUS 4.5 SHIPS.
machine #47 'blocked on review.' typed in 1.0 s: give it ≥1.5 s or cut.
signal #12–#19: the 12 s human-speed establishing run of 2 s shots, which is exactly the slowness the client rejected.
signal #29 (two messages in a 1.0 s gate pass) and signal #101 (two cards in one 2.4 s shot).
signal #71–#78: 6 s of building a dark, unpowered wireframe factory with no payoff.
signal #109: the 8×3 f recall flurry (10 images/s, flash risk). Use 6 f centered recalls as in machine #114–#119.
signal #62: the protagonist cursor becoming the Google-study coordinator.
signal #92/#95/#98/#101: 2.4 s 'read-safe' proof holds at the climax.
'THE OTHER 84%?' (signal #51, wave #44) and 'MORE AGENTS?' (signal #52, wave #45). The derived figure invites the 'that's meetings' rebuttal; machine #49's typed reflex does the job better.
wave #38 / #107: a tsunami breaking over a city of desks with people. It reads as AI wiping out the workforce, which is the wrong brand tone.
wave #39: the drain-back, which implies the first wave receded.
wave #64–#68 cadence: six consecutive 2.0 s card shots.
wave #86: the 'OPUS 5.5' card at 69% (dilutes the title). Also wave #128, an end-card lockup that repeats the title 8 s after the title drop.
wave #110: 'THE WHOLE LINE.', which pays off a line that treatment never builds.
Pseudo-data lamp percentages that viewers will read as adoption stats: wave #29 (80% of the city clay), wave #39 (16% stay lit), signal #30 (1 in 10 clay), signal #33 (half the desks warm).
fact_problems: machine #99 '100-AGENT TEAMS, SELF-ORGANIZED.' rewords the system card's 'picked their own structure'. The rule is shorten, never rephrase or strengthen, so use the verbatim 'PICKED THEIR OWN STRUCTURE.' (as in signal #95 / wave #87).

machine #126 'MADE BY OPUS 5.5 AGENTS. ONE BRIEF.' makes 'with' into 'by' and drops 'human', overstating autonomy. facts.md says 'with Claude Opus 5.5 agents, from one human brief' (signal #116 is exact).

signal #62: the protagonist cursor (the Claude stand-in) becomes the coordinator as the counter rolls 17.2→4.4. That attributes Google Research's generic coordinator result to Claude. machine #90's clay (brand-coloured) coordinator node carries the same subtext. Use a neutral node plus a 'SAME STUDY' tag.

Run-rate ~$9B → $30B+ is company-wide and Anthropic-reported, not coding revenue. All three put it inside the coding-wave / 'capability → budget' beat (machine #25, signal #36, wave #24). Keep the ANTHROPIC-REPORTED whisper legible (≥22 px, ≥0.8 s) and don't render it as the code tower's own output.

machine #35: CODE is station 3 of 7 (#34), but the bar 'sweeps along the line and stops after exactly 16% of its length'. From the line start that lights PLAN, not CODE. Light the CODE segment in place, sized at 16%, and keep the wording a share of developer TIME, not of stations.

'THE OTHER 84%?' (signal #51, wave #44) is derived arithmetic. Atlassian's remaining 84% includes meetings and non-delivery time, so signal #49's labels mapping it onto REVIEW/TEST/DEPLOY/ON-CALL overstate the source.
wave #39 (drain-back) implies the first wave receded. facts.md shows the opposite: budgets, adoption up (JetBrains 18% → ~39%), and the run-rate rising. 16% is a share of dev time, not a retreat.

Uncontrolled percentage-shaped visuals read as data: wave #29 (80% of desks clay), wave #39 (16% stay lit), signal #30 (1 in 10 cursors clay), signal #33 (half the desks warm). They conflict with real figures (JetBrains ~39%; McKinsey ~2 in 10 organizations scaling).

wave #72 '~30,000 AGENTS AT ONCE' is Anthropic-internal (Aug 2026) and predates Opus 5.5 (Sep 22). If it is used, it must stay labelled INSIDE ANTHROPIC, sit away from Opus 5.5 proof cards and never be framed as an Opus 5.5 result.

machine #104–#105 split 'FABLE 5.1-LEVEL WORK.' from '40% LOWER COST THAN OPUS 5. · ANTHROPIC'. The first card stands alone with no source or comparator. Keep the two as one tagged pair (Anthropic claim), and never let the foreman/apex imagery imply Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's most capable model (Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 sit above it).

Gap in all three: the client's closing claim, 'the next wave has started', is carried only by the labelled 2027 projection. facts.md has real evidence that goes unused: Factory raised at $5B (Sep 15 2026), saying 'A move from individual coding agents to software factories.'; AWS Kiro merged 1,000 PRs in 7 days; StrongDM's two dark-factory rules; and 'only a handful' of Level-5 teams. Put one of these, or the labelled ~30,000-agents beat, on screen before the title.
machine #6 'THE NEXT ONE?' and signal #8 'THAT WAS WAVE ONE.' are framing, not claims, and are fine. But no card may assert the next wave has started without one of the sourced proofs above.
